text.p: Alphatec Electronics, listed flagship of Thailand's cash-strapped electronics giant Alphatec Group, is negotiating with ING Bank to restructure its $32 million debt after failing to meet obligations last week.
Pornthep Rohitchat, Alphatec Electronics vice president of finance, told Reuters on Monday that negotiations with ING Bank were expected to be finalised by mid-June.
He also said the company expected to be able to come up with $45 million for put options on its convertible debentures issued on European bond markets which are due on June 22.
"Our negotiation with ING Bank is quite positive. The company had already repaid some of the debt earlier this year. About $26-28 million is left to be paid," he said.
"The condition on debt repayment has to change partly due to our delay in the planned listing on the New York stock market because of the unfavourable economic atmosphere," he said.

Thailand's difficult economic situation has made it tough for the company and Alphatec Group to raise funds. Alphatec Group, the firm's unlisted parent company, was hard hit earlier last month when Texas Instruments of the United States withdrew its investment from two joint venture projects, citing the group's inability to finance its portion in a required time.

The group has already been struggling to find $550 million or more to finish another of its ambitious projects -- the country's first $850 million silicon-chip foundry run by unlisted Submicron Technology Plc.
On the convertible debentures, Pornthep said Alphatec Electronics would do its best to meet the obligations.

The firm issued convertible bonds worth $45 million in 1994. The bond, underwritten by Bankers Trust, is trading at a big discount to face value and analysts said most investors were expected to exercise the put option on June 22.

"We are positive that we will be able to meet obligations should investors decide to exercise the option...But I am not allowed to reveal the financial arrangement as it could derail the negotiations," he said.
"All that I can say is the company is positive on that prospect and that we have a strong intention to see no defaults," Pornthep added.

But banking sources speculated that new financial arrangements being worked out by Alphatec Group could hit snags as lenders would be reluctant to extend credit unless the firm agreed to restructure itself substantially.
